conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity (ci.yml line 137); workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt); cargo deny check advisories licenses bans (ci.yml line 211). New Cargo.lock entries must be >=7 days old unless SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK=true.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> or Vec<String>; no panics; source slicing guarded with get_node_text bounds check (mod.rs). Parser errors are ParserError::UnsupportedLanguage / QueryError / ParseError. Query compile failures are logged once via tracing::error in get_compiled_queries.

patterns: Each language handler file exposes pub const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as raw string S-expressions (java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs).
Handlers are registered in languages/mod.rs get_language_info() as a match arm returning Some(LanguageInfo { ... }) with Option fields for optional handlers (swift.rs, java.rs, css.rs).
get_ts_language() repeats the grammar selection in a second match arm (mod.rs line 317-334).
Extension to language mapping is a flat const EXTENSION_MAP slice of (ext, lang) tuples (lang.rs line 12).

Inheritance: swift.rs walks child(i) and matches child.kind() == 'inheritance_specifier' rather than using field names; java.rs uses child_by_field_name('superclass'/'interfaces'). PHP has no fields for extends/implements, so the Swift kind-based walk is the applicable pattern.

Defuse: capture names are prefixed write., read., writeread.; capture text must equal the symbol name exactly (parser_elements.rs 868-880), so a PHP variable capture must target the inner name node, not variable_name, to exclude the $ sigil.

Element consumer accepts capture names function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name, type_name (parser_elements.rs 282-292); java.rs uses @interface_name which the consumer ignores and falls back to the name field.
Tests per handler: queries_compile (Query::new for each constant), set_language_smoke (parse and assert !has_error), element_query_matches_class_and_function, inheritance happy path and empty case.

approaches.name: A: Mirror Java/Swift handler with grammar LANGUAGE_PHP, kind-based inheritance walk (RECOMMENDED)
approaches.description: Add crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with the five constants and extract_inheritance; pin tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 (fallback 0.25.1 if crates.io publish date fails the 7-day gate); use LANGUAGE_PHP; add php to EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, get_language_info, get_ts_language, pub mod php, README list and count; unit tests in php.rs; one integration test in crates/aptu-coder/tests/. ELEMENT_QUERY captures @function and @class with @func_name, @method_name, @class_name so the existing consumer reads names. DEFUSE captures the inner name node of variable_name so the sigil is excluded.
pros: Matches the Java and Swift registry pattern exactly; the consumer already reads these capture names
Covers every acceptance criterion: five queries, extract_inheritance, HTML template via LANGUAGE_PHP, defuse sites
No new core tree-sitter version: tree-sitter-language 0.1.9 already locked
Grammar node and field names verified against php/src/node-types.json and php/src/grammar.json
cons: The Java extract_inheritance cannot be copied: PHP has no superclass/interfaces fields, so the walk is by child kind (Swift pattern)
Defuse on a bare name also matches same-named functions, classes, and properties (same trade-off as Java identifier matching)
Binary size increases by the PHP grammar parser.c (about 7.5 MB source) compiled into the release binary; delta must be measured for the PR

approaches.name: B: Use LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY grammar for .php files
approaches.description: Same handler as A but register tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY so the grammar has no HTML text rule.
pros: Slightly smaller parse surface; PHP-only files parse without the text rule
cons: Fails the issue acceptance criterion: a .php file mixing HTML and <?php ... ?> must parse with zero ERROR nodes
Real-world .php templates are mixed-mode, so most files would produce ERROR nodes
No dependency benefit: both entry points live in the same crate build

approaches.name: C: Regex-based extractor (no tree-sitter grammar)
approaches.description: Implement a regex scanner for function, class, interface, trait, enum, use and call patterns, following the regex approach used for Astro, CSS, YAML, JSON and TOML in commit 2b32268 (#1069) before the grammar upgrade in 07c50d4 (#1063).
pros: No new Cargo.lock entry, so no 7-day age gate or cargo deny churn
cons: Contradicts the issue: scope requires tree-sitter-php and node kinds from the grammar
Misses structure inside strings and comments; the repo already moved away from regex for CSS and YAML (audit doc 2026-06-unsupported-extension-handling.md line 148)
Cannot support def-use or structural inheritance reliably

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets every acceptance criterion in #1864 (mixed HTML via LANGUAGE_PHP, five query constants, extract_inheritance, def-use sites) and it reuses the existing consumer capture names and the Swift kind-based inheritance pattern. Pin tree-sitter-php to 0.25.2 only after confirming its crates.io publish date is at least 7 days old; otherwise use 0.25.1. Add php to supported_languages() (mandatory; css and yaml are missing from that list, and that gap should not be copied). Keep DEFUSE_QUERY: it is an Option field, so the compiler will not enforce it, but the issue scope requires it and without it extract_def_use returns no sites for PHP.

element_query_draft:
pub const ELEMENT_QUERY: &str = r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
";

Node kinds and captured fields (each verified in php/src/node-types.json):
- function_definition: field name -> name node, capture func_name; outer node captured as function. Free functions only.
- method_declaration: field name -> name node, capture method_name; outer node captured as function.
- class_declaration: field name -> name node, capture class_name; outer node captured as class.
- interface_declaration: field name -> name node, capture class_name; outer node captured as class.
- trait_declaration: field name -> name node, capture class_name; outer node captured as class.
- enum_declaration: field name -> name node, capture class_name; outer node captured as class.
defuse_query_draft:
pub const DEFUSE_QUERY: &str = r"
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(reference_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(simple_parameter name: (variable_name (name) @write.local))
(static_variable_declaration name: (variable_name (name) @write.local))
(augmented_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(update_expression argument: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(variable_name (name) @read.usage)
";

Adapted from java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY, which is:

pub const DEFUSE_QUERY: &str = r"
(local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local))
(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)
(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)
(identifier) @read.usage
";

Why the PHP version differs: PHP has no local declaration keyword, so the local-declaration analogue is simple_parameter and static_variable_declaration. PHP variables are variable_name nodes whose text includes the $ sigil; capturing the inner name child (text without $) lets parser_elements.rs line 870 match the bare symbol name. Capture prefixes write., writeread., read. are required by parser_elements.rs 878-884. Verified in node-types: assignment_expression.left, reference_assignment_expression.left, augmented_assignment_expression.left, update_expression.argument, simple_parameter.name and static_variable_declaration.name all accept variable_name; variable_name has child name.
inheritance_walk_citation:
Source: php/src/grammar.json rules, fetched via gh api repos/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/contents/php/src/grammar.json, and cross-checked with php/src/node-types.json.

class_declaration rule (verbatim structure): SEQ of [ CHOICE(FIELD attributes: attribute_list | BLANK), REPEAT(_modifier), ALIAS 'class' (anonymous), FIELD name: RESERVED(name, context 'classes'), CHOICE(SYMBOL base_clause | BLANK), CHOICE(SYMBOL class_interface_clause | BLANK), FIELD body: declaration_list ].

The walk: (1) start at a class_declaration node; (2) base_clause and class_interface_clause are NOT fields, so iterate node.child(i) for i in 0..child_count() and match child.kind(); (3) for kind == 'base_clause' (the extends list), iterate its named children; each is one of name, qualified_name, relative_name (from the _name rule: CHOICE of name, qualified_name, relative_name alternatives); emit 'extends {text}' for each; (4) for kind == 'class_interface_clause' (the implements list), iterate named children the same way and emit 'implements {text}' for each.

base_clause rule: SEQ [ ALIAS 'extends' (anonymous, named:false), SEQ [ SYMBOL _name, REPEAT(SEQ [ STRING ',', SYMBOL _name ]) ] ]. class_interface_clause rule: SEQ [ ALIAS 'implements' (anonymous), SEQ [ SYMBOL _name, REPEAT(SEQ [ ',', _name ]) ] ]. Keywords are anonymous, so named_child iteration yields only the type names.

Node-level confirmation: class_declaration CHILDREN include base_clause and class_interface_clause (node-types.json); base_clause and class_interface_clause CHILDREN are name, qualified_name, relative_name (multiple). interface_declaration has base_clause only (multiple parent interfaces, emitted as extends). enum_declaration has class_interface_clause (implements) and an optional primitive_type backing type. trait_declaration has no clauses.

Expected output for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B': ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for a class with no clauses: [].
